h: Tonbridge tips and Medway valley extras
p: Tonbridge is easy to reach, sitting on the main railway line between London and the Kent coast, with a busy station near the High Street. Drivers can get there easily from the A21. That makes it handy for a day out with friends or family coming from different directions.

Before you climb, get the participation forms done. Every climber needs one, with a parent or guardian signing for under-18s, and filling it in online saves time on the day. Check the age guidance when booking, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for little ones. Allow a couple of hours for the whole visit.

Got a nervous climber? Start them on a low wall and encourage an early let-go. Feeling how gently the auto-belay lowers you is the best way to calm the nerves. Trainers, comfy clothes and a water bottle are all you need.

When you're done climbing, Haysden Country Park on the western edge of town has lakes, meadows and woodland walks, plus easy paths along the River Medway. Penshurst Place, a few miles west, is a grand medieval manor with famous gardens and an adventure playground. Hever Castle, the childhood home of Anne Boleyn, is a short drive west for gardens, a maze and a lake, while Royal Tunbridge Wells is just down the road for the Pantiles and a bite to eat.
